headline: Character.AI files for bankruptcy, looking to sell assets to Disney
summary: The chatbot startup, once a generative AI boom standout, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and is looking to sell assets to Disney, facing $50M-$100M in liabilities.
details: Character.AI, a prominent generative AI chatbot startup, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US. The company lists estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million as it seeks to sell its assets.

This move comes after the company faced significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds over the past year. Despite these challenges, Character.AI continued to release updates and products for its online bots.

Disney is positioned as the lead bidder for Character.AI's assets, setting a baseline for other potential offers. The entertainment giant would pay $20 million for undisclosed assets and receive a nonexclusive license to unspecified intellectual property.

Disney's involvement follows its recent hiring of Character.AI's former CEO, Karandeep Anand, as its chief technology officer. Disney had previously sent cease and desist letters to Character.AI over unauthorized chatbots of its characters.

The acquisition resembles an 'acquihire' strategy, with Disney also expecting a number of Character.AI's technical team to join its ranks. This mirrors a previous instance where Google acquired much of Character.AI's talent in 2024.

Character.AI expects the sale process to conclude by late November or early December, continuing its services, including paid subscriptions, in the interim. However, the company warned that the platform would be wound down if a suitable bid does not emerge.

headline_marked: Cisco Finesse [[SSRF vulnerability]] won't be patched until 2027
headline: Cisco Finesse SSRF vulnerability won't be patched until 2027
summary: A critical SSRF flaw in Cisco Finesse has no vendor fix available until early 2027, leaving administrators with limited options.
details: A critical Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability, CVE-2026-20362, has been disclosed in Cisco Finesse, the agent desktop for Cisco contact center platforms. Rated 7.2 on CVSS v3, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain limited sensitive information by tricking the server into issuing requests on their behalf.

Unlike most vulnerability advisories, Cisco Finesse will not receive a patch for this flaw until January and February of 2027. Fixed releases include Finesse 15.0(1) SU3, Packaged CCE and Unified CCE 15.0(1)ES202701, and Unified CCX 15.0(1) SU2. Versions 12.6 and earlier require migration.

Cisco states there are no workarounds for this vulnerability, leaving administrators to implement compensating controls. These include keeping the Finesse web interface off untrusted networks and monitoring outbound requests for suspicious destinations.

Administrators are advised to treat reachability to the management interface as the primary control and to document any accepted risks with an owner and review date. Cisco has not reported any malicious use of this vulnerability to date.
